content: Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. For guidance on disposal, consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. This information was last updated in August 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Ertapenem is a carbapenem-type antibiotic used to prevent and treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is administered via injection into a muscle or vein, as directed by your doctor, typically once or twice daily. If used to prevent an infection, it is given intravenously by a healthcare professional. For intramuscular injections, follow the manufacturer’s instructions for mixing with a 1% lidocaine solution. Before use, inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use it if either is present. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. To achieve the best results, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site, as well as upset stomach, headache, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile bacteria, which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before using ertapenem, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other carbapenems (e.g., imipenem), penicillins, cephalosporins, or any other substances. If receiving an intramuscular injection, also disclose any allergies to amide-type local anesthetics (e.g., lidocaine). This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Ertapenem may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). Additionally, this medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. In case of overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests (e.g., complete blood count, kidney function tests) to monitor your progress. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
